info.title: Graph Agent Core API
info.description:
A multi-tenant, multi-domain LangGraph RAG agent. A client starts a turn, reads its events as they stream, answers an approval the
agent asks for, and lists its own past sessions. One graph serves every domain; `X-Domain` picks which (default `ecorp`).

**Who is calling.** Behind the front door (the authlimit service) a client sends `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`; the door
verifies it and gives the API a signed identity, so the tenant and person are never taken from a header or a body. Only a deployment run
with `AUTH_MODE=headers` (a developer's machine, the tests) reads `X-Tenant-Id` and `X-Principal-Id` as sent. Everything a caller reads or
changes is scoped to its tenant and person.

**Errors.** A refusal the application makes is the canonical envelope `{"code", "message", "details"}`; switch on `code`, not on the
text. A turn's own failures arrive as an `error` event on its stream, in the same shape.

**Streams.** `POST /chat/stream/queued` and `GET /ingest/stream/{job_id}` answer with server-sent events, which OpenAPI describes only
as a `text/event-stream` body; the event vocabulary is in the first route's description.

servers.description: This API alone (`make serve`). Runs with AUTH_MODE=headers: name the caller with X-Tenant-Id and X-Principal-Id.
Behind the front door (`make authlimit-up-app`). Send a Casdoor access token as a Bearer token.

get.description:
The built-in web UI (pattern 29) — a single self-contained page, no
build step, no CDN dependency. Talks only to `POST /chat/stream/queued`'s
SSE vocabulary, never a special-cased endpoint of its own. Read from
disk per request (not cached) so editing the file and refreshing is
enough during development — this isn't a hot path.

Liveness only — always 200 if this process can respond at all. See
`GET /health/ready` for whether it can actually complete a turn (see
app/adapters/inbound/api/health.py on why these stay separate endpoints).

Readiness — 200 only if every real dependency is reachable right now,
503 otherwise, with which one(s) failed in the body (see
app/adapters/inbound/api/health.py::check_dependencies).

post.description:
Same SSE event vocabulary an in-process `astream_events_turn` would
produce (token, tool_start, tool_end, citations, followups,
approval_required, error, done), but this process never runs the graph
itself — it publishes the turn onto a shared Redis Stream and streams
back whatever a separate `agent_worker.py` process publishes to this
turn's results stream (pattern 43, app/adapters/outbound/redis/queue.py).

This makes the SSE-serving tier and agent-executing tier independently
scalable: more `uvicorn` processes scale concurrent SSE connections,
more `agent_worker.py` processes scale concurrent turns. Needs at least
one worker running (`make agent-worker`) to ever produce a reply.

A real `approval_required` pause here IS actionable (the worker no
longer auto-declines it), resumed via `POST /chat/resume` below.

`domain` (`X-Domain` header, see `get_domain`) picks which domain's
requests stream this is published onto — only a worker serving that
domain (`AGENT_WORKER_DOMAINS`) reads it, letting one API process serve
every running domain.

Deduplicated against an identical (`thread_id`, `message`, `images`)
resubmission within `CHAT_SUBMIT_DEDUP_TTL_SECONDS`
(`queue.py::claim_or_get_existing_submission`) — a client's own retry
of this exact call reuses the first attempt's `request_id` and SSE
stream rather than publishing (and running) a second, independent
turn. See that function's own docstring for why the thread lock alone
doesn't already cover this.

post.description:
Continue a turn paused at human_approval — the HTTP counterpart to
`astream_events_resume`. Always routed through the same Redis queue as a
new turn (pattern 43), not run in-process: a resume can execute a real
tool call and run more LLM turns, so handling it in the SSE-serving tier
would reintroduce the work `POST /chat/stream/queued` exists to move
off. Any worker in `domain`'s own pool can pick this up — the shared
checkpoint lives in Postgres, not a worker's process memory. `domain`
must match the original turn's (the caller is expected to keep sending
the same `X-Domain` for a given thread_id).

`ctx` is re-supplied here, not reused from the original pause — see
`astream_events_resume`'s own docstring for why. It must belong to the
conversation's owner: `_require_conversation_owner` is checked first, so
approving, rejecting or running another caller's paused action is a 404.

post.description:
Stop a turn, whichever of two states it's in — two independent
mechanisms fire unconditionally (each a no-op if it doesn't apply):

1. Actively streaming — a new turn, or the run that follows an approval
   (`"resume"`): sets a short-lived Redis flag
   (`queue.py::set_cancel_flag`) the worker running that turn polls
   between graph events (`app/agent/runtime/core.py`'s `cancel_check`) — its own
   results stream gets the terminal "cancelled" event directly. Keyed
   by thread_id alone; domain is irrelevant since the worker polls the
   flag directly.
2. Paused at human_approval: publishes a `"cancel"` job (pattern 36's
   `cancel_run`, over `domain`'s own queue) — picked up by any worker in
   that domain's pool.

This endpoint's own SSE response is the job-2 outcome specifically —
not a proxy for job-1's effect on the original turn's stream, which the
caller is expected to already be reading independently.

get.description:
One session's transcript, for the switcher to replay. `session_belongs_to`
is checked FIRST and is the entire authorization boundary — the shared
Postgres checkpointer `get_session_messages` reads has no tenant/
principal/domain of its own to scope by, so skipping this would let any
caller read any thread_id's transcript by guessing ids. `domain` must
match too, extending the same check to a third axis.

get.description:
This caller's own tenant usage — exposes
`spend.usage_summary` (the usage events) over HTTP, so a caller can see how close they are to
MAX_COST_USD_PER_TENANT_PER_DAY without getting refused first. `budgets` adds every limit
that applies to this caller (the tenant's and their own, overrides included).
Tenant-scoped only; no way to query another tenant's spend, or another person's.

`credits` is the tenant's wallet, present only when the deployment has credits on and the tenant has
a wallet (the billing port decides; this endpoint only shows what it is given). Like the budget figures it
does not fail open: an endpoint that cannot read the wallet says so rather than report a calm "no wallet".

post.description:
Upload documents to build this tenant's corpus — PDF/DOCX only today
(app/ingestion/extractors.py); `.txt`/`.md` have their own path
(ingestor.py::ingest_file, the CLI/script-driven one).

Fire-and-forget per file: this handler only gets bytes into MinIO and a
job onto the queue — parsing/embedding happens in ingest_worker.py, on a
SEPARATE queue from chat turns (see ingest_queue.py). Each file's
outcome tracks independently via its own `job_id`
(`GET /ingest/stream/{job_id}`), so one slow/failing file never blocks
the others — including a FAILING one: every per-file problem (bad
extension, too-large, a MinIO/Redis error) is caught and reported back
as that file's own `IngestUploadResult.error`, rather than raising and
losing whatever earlier files in the SAME request already succeeded.

Only "too many files" is rejected synchronously, before touching any
file — a UX/abuse guard on this one call, distinct from
INGEST_WORKER_MAX_CONCURRENCY (it limits how many jobs one submission
creates, not how many a worker runs at once), and genuinely
request-wide rather than per-file.

A file that uploads to MinIO but then fails to publish its own job is
cleaned up (`ObjectStore.delete_object`) rather than left as an
orphaned blob nothing will ever ingest or remove.

get.description:
SSE progress for one upload's job — `{"type": "started"}`, zero or
more `{"type": "progress", "done": N, "total": M}` while
ingest_worker.py's embedding loop runs, then one terminal event:
`{"type": "done", "chunks": N}` or `{"type": "error", ...}`.
Deliberately NOT ownership-checked against app/agent/runtime/sessions.py-style records
(this pipeline keeps no job directory) — `job_id` is a `uuid4().hex`,
unguessable in practice, same posture as the chat results streams.

limit_usd.title: Limit Usd
limit_usd.description: The cap, after any per-tenant or per-person override.

remaining_usd.title: Remaining Usd
remaining_usd.description: What is left, counting in-flight turns for a tenant limit; never below 0.

resets_at.title: Resets At
resets_at.description: When a monthly window next starts from zero; null for the rolling day.

BudgetStatus.title: BudgetStatus
BudgetStatus.description: One spend limit that applies to the caller, with how much of it is used.

thread_id.title: Thread Id
thread_id.description: The conversation's thread id to cancel — whether it's actively streaming right now or paused at human_approval; POST /chat/cancel handles both cases from this one field.

message.title: Message
message.description: The user's message to the agent.

thread_id.title: Thread Id
thread_id.description: Conversation id; reuse it across calls to keep memory.

images.title: Images
images.description: Optional image URLs or data URIs to attach to this turn (GRAPH_PATTERNS.md pattern 44) — passed straight through to whichever model is configured behind CHAT_MODEL; a non-vision-capable model simply can't act on them. Never fetched or decoded by this app itself.

require_approval.title: Require Approval
require_approval.description: Ask for an approval before EVERY tool call, read-only ones included (`make chat-hitl`). Can only add approvals.

unattended.title: Unattended
unattended.description: Nobody can answer an approval (the Telegram channel): the worker declines a pause and never approves it, and the conversation is left ready for the next message (GRAPH_PATTERNS.md 89).

replay_key.title: Replay Key
replay_key.description: Makes this request one attempt however often it is sent: a second request for the same conversation with the same key streams the FIRST attempt's turn and starts none, for as long as its results stream lives. Scoped to the conversation, and so to its owner.

available.title: Available
available.description: What may still be consumed right now: live (unexpired) credits minus any debt. Can be negative.

debt.title: Debt
debt.description: Credits consumed beyond the balance, repaid first by the next grant; 0 if none.

ledger.title: Ledger
ledger.description: Every lot including expired ones not yet swept, plus debt: the ledger's own total.

enforced.title: Enforced
enforced.description: Whether a turn is refused (insufficient_credits) when `available` is not positive.

CreditBalance.title: CreditBalance
CreditBalance.description:
The caller's tenant's wallet (packages/billing/src/credit_billing/credits.py). Exact decimals, serialised as strings:
a JSON number would round-trip through a float and a balance must not drift.

job_id.title: Job Id
job_id.description: Poll/stream this at GET /ingest/stream/{job_id}. None if this file failed.

error.title: Error
error.description: Set instead of job_id if THIS file failed (bad type, upload, or publish failure) — other files in the same request still succeed independently; see ingest_upload's own docstring.

tool_calls.title: Tool Calls
tool_calls.description: The tool call(s) awaiting approval, same shape as the approval_required SSE event.

resumable.title: Resumable
resumable.description: False if this checkpoint's state_schema_version no longer matches the running build — approve/reject would be refused; the caller should show it as unresumable, not a working button.

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.description: Conditions worth a person's attention that do NOT make the API unready: an embedding-identity mismatch (retrieval from that collection is refused and degrades, but turns still run), a legacy collection adopted without proof, an ML-service model that is down. Never changes `status` or the HTTP code.

ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse
ReadinessResponse.description:
GET /health/ready's body — see app/adapters/inbound/api/health.py's module docstring for
why this is a separate question from GET /health's liveness probe.

approved.title: Approved
approved.description: Approve (true) or reject (false) the pending tool call(s).

role.title: Role
role.description: "user" or "assistant", or "system" for a compact_history breadcrumb noting that older turns were trimmed/summarized.

thread_id.title: Thread Id
thread_id.description: Reuse as ChatRequest.thread_id to continue this session.

title.title: Title
title.description: The opening message that started this session, truncated.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: When this thread_id was first seen.

last_active_at.title: Last Active At
last_active_at.description: Most recent turn on this thread_id.

total_tokens.title: Total Tokens
total_tokens.description: All-time tokens recorded for this tenant.

total_cost_usd.title: Total Cost Usd
total_cost_usd.description: All-time cost (USD) recorded for this tenant.

last_24h_cost_usd.title: Last 24H Cost Usd
last_24h_cost_usd.description: Cost recorded in the last rolling 24h — what the daily budget check sees.

daily_budget_usd.title: Daily Budget Usd
daily_budget_usd.description: MAX_COST_USD_PER_TENANT_PER_DAY — the ceiling last_24h_cost_usd is checked against.

budgets.title: Budgets
budgets.description: Every spend limit that applies to THIS caller — the tenant's and the caller's own, overrides included — with how much is used, so they can see how close they are before being refused. Only the caller's own personal figures; never another person's.

credits.description: The tenant's credit wallet, or null when the deployment has credits off or this tenant has no wallet (it is then never charged or gated). Tenant-wide, like the cost figures above.

UsageResponse.title: UsageResponse
UsageResponse.description:
GET /usage's body — this caller's tenant, all-time plus the same
rolling-24h number budgets.check_tenant_daily checks, so a caller can see
how close they are to the daily budget without getting refused first.

tags.name: chat

tags.name: usage
tags.description: The caller's tenant spend and the limits that apply to it.

tags.name: ingest
